transcript.user_1_turn_1: I'm naming a podcast episode about a very awkward first day at work. Nothing actually went wrong; I just managed to look confused for eight straight hours.
transcript.user_2_turn_1: So we're aiming for embarrassing, not 'HR has opened an investigation.'
transcript.user_1_turn_2: Exactly. First-Day Fumbles is fine, but it feels like a title I've seen a hundred times.
transcript.user_2_turn_2: Yeah, it explains the premise but doesn't really have a punchline.
transcript.user_1_turn_3: I also had Hello, HR and Name-Tag Panic. I like short titles because they don't get chopped off in the podcast app.
transcript.user_2_turn_3: Those are cleaner. Hello, HR is dry; Name-Tag Panic tells you the kind of awkwardness immediately.
transcript.user_1_turn_4: Give me one wildcard that sounds even less polished.
transcript.user_2_turn_4: How about Oops, I'm New? Tiny, self-explanatory, and it sounds like someone trying to recover in real time.
transcript.user_1_turn_5: Okay, that's annoyingly good. I think that one actually makes me laugh when I picture the episode thumbnail.
